title: the booking schema from the schema interview: what the constraints refuse, and what each tenant sees

steps.sql: INSERT INTO bookings (hotel_id, room_id, guest_id, stay) VALUES (1, 1, 2, '[2026-12-24,2026-12-29)')
steps.note: room 101 is already booked from the 20th to the 27th. an overlapping stay is refused by the exclusion constraint, with the conflicting row in the message.

error.message: conflicting key value violates exclusion constraint "bookings_room_id_stay_excl"
error.detail: Key (room_id, stay)=(1, [2026-12-24,2026-12-29)) conflicts with existing key (room_id, stay)=(1, [2026-12-20,2026-12-27)).

steps.sql: INSERT INTO bookings (hotel_id, room_id, guest_id, stay) VALUES (1, 1, 2, '[2026-12-27,2026-12-30)') RETURNING id, room_id, stay
steps.note: a stay that starts the day the last one ends doesn't overlap: [) ranges include the first day and exclude the last.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO bookings (hotel_id, room_id, guest_id, stay) VALUES (1, 2, 1, '[2026-12-22,2026-12-25)') RETURNING id, room_id, stay
steps.note: room 102 has a booking for the same dates, but it was cancelled, and the constraint only looks at confirmed rows.

steps.sql: INSERT INTO bookings (hotel_id, room_id, guest_id, stay) VALUES (1, 1, 1, '[2026-12-31,2026-12-31)')
steps.note: an empty stay (checking out the day you check in) is refused by the CHECK.

error.message: new row for relation "bookings" violates check constraint "bookings_stay_check"

steps.note: rates use a temporal primary key: room 101 can't have two prices for the same night.

error.message: conflicting key value violates exclusion constraint "room_rates_pkey"
error.detail: Key (room_id, valid)=(1, [2026-12-24,2026-12-26)) conflicts with existing key (room_id, valid)=(1, [2026-12-01,2027-01-01)).

steps.note: the app connects as booking_app with hotel 1 in a setting. row-level security shows it hotel 1's bookings only.

steps.sql:
SELECT set_config('app.hotel_id', '2', false) IS NOT NULL AS set;
SELECT id, hotel_id, room_id, stay, status FROM bookings ORDER BY id
steps.note: the same query with hotel 2 in the setting: only the old mill's one booking.

steps.sql:
SELECT set_config('app.hotel_id', '', false) IS NOT NULL AS set;
SELECT id, hotel_id, room_id, stay, status FROM bookings ORDER BY id
steps.note: with no hotel set, the policy compares against NULL, which is never true: no rows, not all rows.

steps.sql:
SELECT set_config('app.hotel_id', '2', false) IS NOT NULL AS set;
INSERT INTO bookings (hotel_id, room_id, guest_id, stay) VALUES (1, 1, 1, '[2027-01-02,2027-01-04)')
steps.note: hotel 2's app tries to write a booking for hotel 1. the policy's USING also checks new rows, and refuses.

error.message: new row violates row-level security policy for table "bookings"
